title: Anchored Scope & Readiness Lab — Customer Workshop Facilitation Guide
body:
Purpose:
This working guide is for a 3-hour customer-facing ‘Anchored Scope & Readiness Lab’ to accelerate alignment on production constraints, acceptance criteria, and the minimal POC that demonstrates deployment feasibility. Focus is on making trade-offs explicit (latency vs. cost vs. accuracy) and producing a concrete, timeboxed next-step plan that both engineering and product stakeholders can sign off on.

Audience:
- Customer engineering leads (2–4)
- Product/PM (1–2)
- Customer security/compliance rep (optional)
- Redwood SEs: facilitator + 1 technical lead + 1 solutions engineer

Pre-Work (sent 72h before):
- Intake form responses (system architecture diagram, expected QPS, SLOs, data sensitivity class). Link in linked_artifacts.
- Short sample payload (50–200 examples) and 3–5 hard success/failure cases.
- Customer to confirm which cloud/VPC/private deployment category they expect (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Redwood to prepare: model variant options (2), estimated baseline latency and cost table for those options, and a proposed fallback flow.

Agenda (3 hours) — timeboxed with outcomes:
0:00–0:15 — Welcome & Anchoring
- Quick intros, roles, constraints.
- Read out intake highlights (owner: Maya) and confirm missing assumptions.
Outcome: Shared list of unknowns to resolve during session.

0:15–0:45 — Business outcome & acceptance criteria workshop
- Round-robin: customer articulates success metrics (e.g., 95p latency, accuracy threshold, error tolerance).
- Capture primary/secondary KPIs and non-functional constraints (data residency, encryption, audit logs).
Outcome: Draft acceptance criteria (1–3 bullet KPIs).

0:45–1:15 — Technical surface mapping (whiteboard)
- Walk through customer architecture diagram. Identify ingress points, throughput expectations, request size distributions, and sensitive data flow.
- Annotate zones where Redwood components would sit (API gateway, routing policy, cache, KV store, models).
Outcome: Deployment topology sketch and integration checklist.

1:15–1:30 — Break

1:30–2:00 — Model and runtime tradeoff rapid teardown
- Present 2 model candidates (e.g., open Llama-variant quantized 4-bit vs. a slightly larger 8-bit variant) + a small hosted fallback. Include expected median p95 latencies and token cost estimates.
- Discuss impact of batching, caching, and KV reuse on latency/cost.
Facilitator note: show a simple table with 3 scenarios: low-latency, cost-optimized, mixed.
Outcome: Agreed primary runtime configuration for the POC plus fallback policy.

2:00–2:30 — Simulated request flow and failure modes
- Walk through 3 user stories with sample requests from pre-work. For each, simulate normal, high-load, and degraded network cases.
- Decide on graceful degradation policy (fallback model, regional reroute, capacity burst).
Outcome: Failure-mode playbook and guardrails for POC.

2:30–2:50 — Hands-on breakout: integration checklist & quick runbook
- Split into two breakout groups (customer infra + SEs). Produce a prioritized task list for the first 2-week POC sprint: infra hooks, secrets/KMS, sample data ingestion, telemetry hooks, success eval harness.
Outcome: Draft 10-item POC sprint backlog with owners and 2-week milestone.

2:50–3:00 — Close & Next Steps
- Confirm owners, quick wins, and date for POC kick-off. Capture any follow-ups and blockers.
Outcome: Signed-off POC charter and kick-off calendar invite.

Slide outline (6–8 slides) — presentable as a short deck
- Slide 1: Title + Objective + Attendees + Timebox
- Slide 2: Synthesis of intake (architecture, QPS, data sensitivity)
- Slide 3: Success metrics & acceptance criteria (visual KPIs)
- Slide 4: Candidate models/runtime options & quick tradeoff table (latency/cost/quality)
- Slide 5: Deployment topology sketch (where Redwood components live)
- Slide 6: Failure-mode playbook (3 scenarios + response)
- Slide 7: 2-week POC sprint backlog (prioritized tasks + owners)
- Slide 8: Sign-offs & next milestones

Facilitation notes & dos/don’ts:
- DO keep the group anchored to acceptance criteria; redirect tangents back to what will move the POC forward.
- DO surface assumptions explicitly and mark them ‘action item to validate’ if unresolved.
- DON’T design final security architecture in the session — capture constraints and schedule a follow-up with security SME.
- DO use timeboxes strictly for breakout exercises; assign a reporter to present outcomes.
- DO call out preferred endpoints for telemetry (e.g., Console route + Prometheus metric names) and confirm agreement to share test metrics during POC.
- DO keep language simple when discussing quantization/bit-width — customers often care about effects, not terminology.

Prep checklist for Redwood SEs (before session):
- Confirm intake diagram read and annotate questions.
- Build two concise model-option summaries with estimated latency/cost numbers.
- Prepare slide with 3-scenario cost/latency table.
- Template POC backlog (Jira ticket seed) and a short eval harness (script skeleton) for quality checks.
- Create a telemetry sample dashboard link and demo data to show during session.

Artifacts produced during session (expected):
- Signed POC charter (one-paragraph objective + 3 acceptance criteria)
- 2-week POC backlog exported to Jira/Linear (10 items)
- Topology sketch image (png) and a short failure-mode playbook doc
- Owner list and scheduled kick-off meeting invite

Common risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Customer cannot share realistic sample data (Mitigation: use synthetic-but-structured payloads and flag evaluation caveats).
- Risk: Security/compliance blockers surface late (Mitigation: identify early and escalate to security SME; offer a dedicated private-deploy discovery session).
- Risk: Expectation mismatch on what POC proves (Mitigation: make acceptance criteria explicit in charter and get signatures).

Follow-ups & success criteria for REDWOOD internal tracking:
- POC kickoff occurred within 7 days of workshop.
- First smoke test (end-to-end request) within 10 days.
- Telemetry streaming with baseline metrics within 14 days.
- Customer verifies at least one acceptance KPI by end of POC sprint.

Appendix: Sample prompts / test cases (from customer pre-work)
- Prompt A (support chat): "Customer: I can't see my billing invoice for March. Assistant: Provide the path and ask for verification details." Expected: Structured response with invoice path + next steps.
- Prompt B (summary): "Summarize the attached policy doc to an executive in 3 bullets." Expected: High-level summary; accuracy checks against 3 anchor sentences.
- Prompt C (classification): "Given user message, return category: billing|technical|other." Expected: >95% agreement with human labels.

Notes about uniqueness of POC deliverable:
- Emphasize that the deliverable is not a full production integration but a validated path with a reproducible smoke-test, telemetry, and a measurable acceptance rubric.
- Keep the POC narrow: instrument one route end-to-end and validate one or two KPIs rather than attempting a complete migration.

Contact & escalation:
- Primary SE: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai)
- Technical lead: Evan Malik (evan@redwood.ai)
- Solutions lead for deployment: Priya Singh (priya@redwood.ai)

End of working guide.

(Internal note: archive final charter under CONFLUENCE-1234 and link Jira-SE-9876 to the POC backlog)
